## What changes the price

The version. On-demand, the PCIe 80 GB starts at $1.99, the NVL 94 GB starts at $2.59 and the SXM 80 GB starts at $2.69. PCIe is a card that fits a standard server slot. It runs at lower power than SXM and links to other GPUs more slowly, and it is usually the cheaper version to rent. NVL is a PCIe card made to be paired with a second one over an NVLink bridge, so the two share data quickly. It draws less power than the SXM version. SXM is a module mounted on NVIDIA's HGX board, where GPUs share data over NVLink. It runs at full power with the fastest links between GPUs, which is why 8-GPU training machines use it.

The pricing type. The cheapest spot price, $1.29 at Azure, is 35% below the cheapest on-demand price. Spot capacity can be taken back at short notice; see spot or on-demand.

The provider. Each provider's cheapest on-demand price runs from $1.99 at RunPod to $6.98 at Azure: 3.5 times as much for the same GPU family.

...

## A month of H100 time

One H100 for a month of 730 hours costs $1,453 at the cheapest on-demand price. On spot it is $942, if the capacity is not taken back. Eight of them for the same month come to $11,622 at that rate; the cheapest whole eight-GPU machine listed here, p5.48xlarge at AWS, is $40,179.

results.title: Spot vs on-demand GPU prices (Nov 2026): 14%–82% less
highlights:
Spot vs on-demand GPU prices (Nov 2026): 14%–82% less

# Spot or on-demand GPUs

What spot GPUs save against on-demand, GPU by GPU, and what you give up for it.

Prices as of 14 Nov 2026, 00:51 UTC

Spot capacity is spare capacity a cloud rents for less, on the condition that it can take it back at short notice. Across the 14 GPUs listed here with both prices, spot runs from 14% to 82% below on-demand.

## How much less spot costs

The cheapest on-demand and the cheapest spot price for each GPU, per GPU per hour. The two can come from different providers.

| GPU | Cheapest on-demand | Cheapest spot | Spot is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AMD Radeon PRO V710 | $2.00 Azure | $0.370 Azure | 82% less |
| AMD Radeon PRO V620 | $2.54 Azure | $0.469 Azure | 82% less |
| NVIDIA A10 | $3.20 Azure | $0.591 Azure | 82% less |
| NVIDIA T4 | $0.526 Azure | $0.149 Azure | 72% less |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | $3.36 AWS | $1.02 Azure | 70% less |
| NVIDIA B200 | $7.99 RunPod | $2.70 Nebius | 66% less |
| NVIDIA B300 | $8.29 Scaleway | $3.75 Nebius | 55% less |
| AMD MI300X | $2.39 RunPod | $1.11 Azure | 54% less |
| NVIDIA H100 | $1.99 RunPod | $1.29 Azure | 35% less |
| NVIDIA A100 | $1.00 RunPod | $0.679 Azure | 32% less |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | $1.69 RunPod | $1.38 Nebius | 18% less |
| NVIDIA H200 | $3.59 RunPod | $3.08 Nebius | 14% less |
| NVIDIA GB200 Grace Blackwell | $27.04 Azure | $27.04 Azure | no saving |
| NVIDIA L40S | $0.790 RunPod | $1.49 Vultr | no saving |

...

Notice before the machine is taken back differs. Azure evicts Spot VMs with up to 30 seconds' notice (Azure ↗). Nebius sends a stop signal 60 seconds before stopping a preemptible VM (Nebius ↗). Nebius spot prices also move hour by hour: each Nebius GPU page here charts them by region, for example the H100.

...

Spot suits work that can stop and carry on: batch jobs, rendering, training that saves a checkpoint every few minutes to storage outside the machine, experiments, and inference behind a queue that retries a failed request.

On-demand is worth its price for long training runs that cannot restart cheaply, interactive work, demos, and anything with a deadline. Thirty or sixty seconds is not enough time to save a large model's state, so a spot job needs its checkpoints already written when the notice comes.

results.title: GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026 · EverXCloud
highlights:
# GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026

Public GPU-hour prices for H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S, RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 across 16 cloud providers, with medians and spreads.

## Executive summary

EverXCloud read the public pricing pages of 16 GPU cloud providers on 2026-10-26 and recorded 75 prices per GPU-hour for eight GPUs. On-demand prices for the same GPU still vary widely between providers, and spot, preemptible or community capacity costs far less than on-demand capacity.

This report covers third-party list prices only. Once the EverXCloud Marketplace launches, its own price index will be published from real transactions.

## Key findings

1. The median on-demand H100 SXM price across 11 providers is $3.99 per GPU-hour, from $3.14 to $6.16: the most expensive listing costs 2.0× the cheapest.
2. Spot, preemptible and community H100 SXM capacity has a median of $2.30 per GPU-hour across 3 providers, 42% below the on-demand median.
3. The H200 carries a 24% premium over the H100 SXM at the median ($4.94 vs $3.99 on demand, 10 providers).
4. On-demand B200 prices range from $6.00 to $8.60 per GPU-hour across 7 providers, with a median of $8.19.
5. The A100 80GB shows the widest relative spread among data center GPUs: 2.6× between the cheapest ($1.09) and the most expensive ($2.79) on-demand listing, across 9 providers.
6. AWS Capacity Blocks, a short-term reservation, list the H100 at $5.97 and the B200 at $14.21 per GPU-hour, 1.5× and 1.7× the on-demand medians of the other providers.

## Prices by GPU

On-demand, USD per GPU-hour

| GPU | Min | Median | Max | Max ÷ min | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.14 | $3.99 | $6.16 | 2.0× | 11 |
| H100 PCIe | $2.89 | $3.29 | $3.50 | 1.2× | 3 |
| H200 | $3.62 | $4.94 | $6.30 | 1.7× | 10 |
| B200 | $6.00 | $8.19 | $8.60 | 1.4× | 7 |
| A100 80GB | $1.09 | $1.49 | $2.79 | 2.6× | 9 |
| L40S | $0.97 | $1.56 | $2.25 | 2.3× | 6 |
| RTX 4090 | $0.39 | $0.64 | $0.89 | 2.3× | 3 |
| RTX 5090 | $0.65 | $0.92 | $1.19 | 1.8× | 2 |

...

## Methodology

- Prices were read on 2026-10-26 on each provider's official public pricing page, in USD per GPU-hour, excluding tax. No price was estimated, negotiated or taken from a third-party aggregator.
- One price per provider, GPU and offer type. When a provider lists several configurations for the same GPU, the lowest listed price was kept, and the listing is recorded in the data.
- Multi-GPU instances are converted to a per-GPU price by dividing the instance price by the number of GPUs (for example CoreWeave and AWS 8-GPU instances).
- On-demand and spot, preemptible or community prices are reported separately. AWS prices are Capacity Block rates, a short-term reservation, and are not included in the on-demand statistics.
- Providers whose pricing page could not be read, showed prices only after sign-in or on request, or did not map prices to GPUs unambiguously were left out: Vast.ai, Crusoe, Vultr, TensorDock, Fluidstack, Genesis Cloud, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Voltage Park, Cudo Compute, Scaleway, Paperspace and SF Compute.
- The median of an even number of prices is the mean of the two middle values.

results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in October 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
After a summer of falling floors, October pauses: H100 ~$2/hr, H200 ~$3+, the B200 in-stock floor flat near $3.75 — but a typical on-demand B200 now rents at ~$8. The floor stopped falling.

...

- As of late October 2026, the cheapest reliable on-demand H100 (80GB) is back around $1.99/GPU-hr (Voltage Park), with brand-name specialty clouds at ~$2.50 (Hyperstack PCIe), ~$2.89 (RunPod), and ~$2.90 SXM (Ori); the median 'cheapest' across two dozen providers is ~$3.33, and spot dips to ~$0.94 (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler H100 is still ~$10–13/hr.
- H200 (141GB) firmed since September: neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99 (Prime Intellect ~$3.14, Spheron ~$3.35, Theta ~$3.69, Hyperbolic ~$3.99), the Ornn transacted index settled at $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 is ~$7.91–13.78.
- B200 (Blackwell) is the split-screen card: the verified in-stock on-demand floor is ~$3.75 (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70 — but the on-demand MEDIAN is now ~$7.99–8.19 (RunPod $7.99, Together $8.19). Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr).
- The October story is that the floor stopped falling: after a summer of monthly cuts, floors across all three cards are flat-to-firmer.
- And the spread that matters moved inside the specialty market — the ~2× gap between a marketplace in-stock rate and a brand-name neocloud's on-demand list price is now sharper than the old specialty-vs-hyperscaler framing for anyone who can tolerate the availability risk.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

| GPU | Cheapest reliable on-demand | Typical on-demand (median) | Hyperscaler on-demand | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.99/hr (Voltage Park), ~$2.50 PCIe (Hyperstack) | ~$3.33/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |
| H200 (141GB) | ~$3.14/hr (Prime Intellect), ~$3.35 (Spheron) | ~$5.00–5.24/hr | ~$7.91–13.78/hr | Bigger context, larger models on one card |
| B200 (Blackwell) | ~$3.75/hr in-stock (Packet.ai) | ~$7.99–8.19/hr | ~$14–16/hr | Frontier-size inference, heavy training |
| GB200 / B300 | ~$8/hr and up, much is quote-only | varies widely | ~$16–27/hr | Largest models, frontier training |

...

If you read one line: a reliable on-demand H100 is ~$1.99–2.90/GPU-hr, an H200 ~$3.14–5/hr, and a B200 is either ~$3.75 or ~$8 depending on whether you mean the cheapest in-stock rate or the typical one — and the decision that saves you the most money still isn't which card, it's whether your GPU is busy enough to rent one at all.

...

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the last week of October 2026 from public pricing pages and multi-provider trackers (getdeploying, Ornn, gpuperhour, Spheron, and vendor pages). GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. The cheapest reliable on-demand rate is back near $1.99/hr (Voltage Park), with ~$2.50 PCIe at Hyperstack, ~$2.89 at RunPod, and ~$2.90 SXM at Ori. The median "cheapest across providers" is ~$3.33. Spot dips near $0.94/hr (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, and firmer than September. Neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99/hr (~$3.14 Prime Intellect, ~$3.35 Spheron, ~$3.69 Theta, ~$3.99 Hyperbolic). The Ornn transacted index — settled daily from real neocloud deals — printed $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 runs ~$7.91–13.78 (Thunder Compute: AWS ~$7.91–9.89, Azure ~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell, 180GB) — the split-screen card. The cheapest verified in-stock on-demand rate is ~$3.75/hr (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70. But the on-demand median is now ~$7.99–8.19: RunPod lists $7.99/hr and Together ~$8.19/hr. Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr). Hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 — the Grace-Blackwell superchips remain premium and partly quote-only: roughly $8/hr and up where published, ~$16–27 at the hyperscalers. If you need one, you're negotiating, not shopping a list.

September's headline was "the B200 floor cracked below $4." October's is quieter and more important: it didn't crack any further. The era of "wait a month, it'll be cheaper" just paused.

...

1. The floor stopped falling. ... The B200 in-stock floor is flat at ~$3.75. For the first monthly map all year, the cheap end didn't get cheaper.
2. H200 firmed.

...

3. The spread moved inside the specialty market. The gap that defined the summer was specialty-vs-hyperscaler (still a real 5–7×).

results.title: How Is Cloud GPU Rental Priced? H100, H200, B200 and B300 Compared | EffectStory
results.author: James Lin
highlights:
SHORT ANSWER

A cloud GPU hour is priced either per whole machine or per GPU, and some systems have no public on-demand price from any provider checked here. To compare H100, H200, B200 and B300 fairly, convert every quote to a per-GPU hour, then check what is bundled and how the capacity is bought.

The principles don't expire; products and figures cited are as of October 2026 and are updated, with dates, when things change.

The price of a cloud GPU hour depends on two things before it depends on the GPU itself: what the quote covers (a whole machine or one GPU) and how the capacity is bought. This guide explains both, then lists published prices for H100, H200, B200 and B300.

...

It depends on the provider: some quote a whole machine per hour, others a single GPU per hour. Google Cloud bills an A4 instance (NVIDIA B200) for its attached GPUs, predefined vCPUs, memory and bundled Local SSD together. Hyperdisk and network usage are billed separately. ⁠ [1] AWS's EC2 on-demand data likewise lists one hourly price per instance size. ⁠ [2]

...

The prices below are US-dollar list prices per hour from each provider's own pricing page or data feed. AWS's data was published on 23 October 2026, and RunPod's page was last updated on 27 August 2026. CoreWeave figures are for North America, and AWS figures are for US East (N. Virginia) on Linux. ⁠ [2]⁠ [6]⁠ [3]

Nebius lists HGX H200 at $5.40 per GPU-hour on demand, with preemptible rates from $0.79. ⁠ [5] For comparison, Nebius's own HGX H100 on-demand rate is $4.50. ⁠ [5]

highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.
